search.purpose: Search Stripe charges, customers, and subscriptions by free-form query string and return ranked smart-id results.
when_to_use: User asks to find a Stripe object by name, email, or descriptor without knowing its ID
Disambiguating between similarly-named entities before calling fetch()
when_not_to_use: Listing every object in a collection — use list_objects() with collection set
Fetching a known object by smart-id — use fetch() directly
limitations: Best-effort substring match across name, email, and metadata fields only
Returns at most 25 ranked results per call
search.parameter_overview: Required: query (free-form string). Returns: ranked array of smart-id results across charges, customers, and subscriptions.

fetch.purpose: Fetch a single Stripe object by smart-id and return its complete representation.
when_to_use: Smart-id is already known from a prior search() or list_objects() call
Need full object payload including nested fields not surfaced in list views
limitations: Single-object fetch only; for batch reads use list_objects()
Returns 404 if smart-id refers to a deleted or expired object
fetch.parameter_overview: Required: id (smart-id of format stripe-api:{type}:{collection}:{identifier}). Returns: full upstream object.

list_collections.purpose: List the available Stripe object collections (Charge, Customer, Subscription, Refund) for discovery.
when_to_use: Discovering what types of data this server exposes before issuing list_objects() calls
Building a collection picker in a UI
limitations: Returns only collection metadata (names + counts), not the objects themselves
Counts are upstream-best-effort — do not rely on exact accuracy for pagination math
list_collections.parameter_overview: No required parameters. Returns: array of collection descriptors with name and approximate object count.

list_objects.purpose: List Stripe objects in a given collection with cursor-based pagination, optionally filtered.
when_to_use: Browsing all charges, customers, or subscriptions in a collection
Walking large datasets via cursor pagination
limitations: Default page size is 25, max 100 per call
Cursor token expires within 24 hours of issuance
list_objects.parameter_overview: Required: collection (one of Charge/Customer/Subscription/Refund). Optional: limit, cursor. Returns: paged array of smart-id results.

upsert.purpose: Create a new Stripe object, or update an existing one when id is provided.
when_to_use: Creating a new charge, customer, or subscription from collected data
Updating metadata or other mutable fields on an existing object by smart-id
when_not_to_use: Deleting an object — use delete() instead
Performing custom action verbs (capture, refund, cancel) — use the dedicated action tools
limitations: Upstream Stripe API may reject creates that violate account constraints (currency, region, KYC)
Partial updates merge into existing object; pass full nested objects to replace them
upsert.parameter_overview: Required: data (object payload). Optional: id (smart-id; presence triggers update path). Returns: created or updated object.

delete.purpose: Permanently delete a Stripe customer object by smart-id.
when_to_use: Purging a customer record after closing an account
GDPR right-to-erasure deletion of personal data
limitations: Only customer deletion is supported; charges and subscriptions cannot be hard-deleted
Deletion is irreversible; consider archiving via metadata first if rollback is needed
delete.parameter_overview: Required: id (customer smart-id). Returns: confirmation envelope with the deleted object id.

charges_capture.purpose: Capture a previously-authorized but uncaptured Stripe charge.
when_to_use: Finalizing a two-step authorize-then-capture flow once goods ship or service starts
Capturing an authorization before the 7-day Stripe expiry
limitations: Charge MUST be in authorized but not yet captured state
Cannot capture more than the originally authorized amount
charges_capture.parameter_overview: Required: charge (smart-id of the authorized charge). Returns: the captured charge object.

charges_refund.purpose: Issue a full or partial refund against a previously-captured Stripe charge.
when_to_use: Customer requests refund for a paid charge
Reversing a captured charge after dispute resolution
limitations: Cannot refund more than the captured amount minus prior refunds
Refund processing is asynchronous; the returned object reflects pending status until upstream settles
charges_refund.parameter_overview: Required: charge (smart-id). Optional: amount (cents; full refund if omitted). Returns: refund object with status.

subscriptions_cancel.purpose: Cancel a Stripe subscription, optionally at period end rather than immediately.
when_to_use: Customer requests cancellation of an active subscription
Pruning subscriptions for a deleted account
limitations: Already-canceled subscriptions return their terminal state without further action
Default behaviour is immediate cancellation with proration
subscriptions_cancel.parameter_overview: Required: subscription_exposed_id (smart-id). Optional: at_period_end (boolean). Returns: canceled subscription object.
